questions.stem: Nitrate, NO3−, is planar and has three equivalent N–O bonds. Its three conventional Lewis contributors place one N=O bond in different positions. Choose between a permanently localised single/double-bond picture and a delocalised pi description. Explain which observations discriminate between them, and state separately the introductory sigma-framework hybridisation model at nitrogen.

answer.summary: The supplied three equivalent N-O bonds support a delocalised pi description rather than a permanently localised one-double/two-single pattern. Separately, nitrogen has three local sigma directions/electron domains and is described as sp2 in the introductory sigma-framework model, leaving an unhybridised p orbital for the pi description.

The contributors are formal components, not structures the ion switches between in time.

questions.stem: For propadiene (allene), H2C=C=CH2, apply local electron-domain counting at each of the three carbon atoms. Assign the introductory hybridisation of each carbon and show how the two mutually perpendicular unhybridised p orbitals on the central carbon constrain the relative planes of the terminal CH2 groups.

answer.summary: Each terminal carbon has three sigma directions and is described as sp2 with one unhybridised p orbital. The central carbon has two sigma directions and is described as sp, leaving two mutually perpendicular unhybridised p orbitals. Each central p orbital overlaps with a terminal p orbital, so the two terminal p axes and terminal CH2 planes are mutually perpendicular.

questions.stem: Ethene is planar; propadiene has terminal CH2 groups in perpendicular planes. Build a connected account from each carbon's local sigma framework, the required pi overlaps and the p-orbital directions. Explain why copying the planar ethene sketch to allene fails.

answer.summary: In ethene, each carbon is locally sp2 and leaves one p orbital; the two p orbitals must be parallel for one pi bond, consistent with a planar carbon framework. In allene, the central carbon is locally sp and leaves two mutually perpendicular p orbitals. Each overlaps with a p orbital on a different terminal sp2 carbon, so the two terminal CH2 planes are perpendicular. Copying ethene's plane to allene ignores the need for two independent orthogonal pi overlaps at the same central atom.

questions.stem: For the benchmark, use these supplied simplified observations, not an exam-source claim: CO2 is linear with two equivalent C–O bonds; NO3− is planar with three equivalent N–O bonds; NH3 is pyramidal with three equivalent N–H bonds. Assess the claim 'Equivalent bonds imply sp2 at the central atom.' Use counterexamples and valid warrants, and distinguish equivalence, electron-domain count and hybridisation as a model description.

answer.summary: The claim is false. CO2 has two equivalent C-O bonds but two central sigma directions/electron domains and is described as sp. NH3 has three equivalent N-H bonds but four local electron domains including the lone pair and is described as sp3. Nitrate N has three sigma directions and is described as sp2, but equivalence is not the criterion. Hybridisation is an atom-local sigma-framework model; bond equivalence is a distinct structural/electronic property.

inputs: supplied benchmark stem and prior move

reasoning_route.why_valid: Nitrogen has four electron domains including the lone pair, so the local introductory model is sp3 despite equivalent N-H bonds.
inputs: supplied benchmark stem and prior move

reasoning_route.why_valid: The species separate bond equivalence from local domain geometry.
inputs: supplied benchmark stem and prior move

reasoning_route.action: Replace the heuristic with atom-local domain counting plus orbital consistency.
reasoning_route.why_valid: Hybridisation describes a local sigma-framework model; equivalence is a separate property.
inputs: supplied benchmark stem and prior move

questions.stem: Compare rotation about the central C–C bond in ethane with twisting about the C=C bond in ethene. Use the sigma and pi overlap arrangements to explain which overlap is altered by each motion. Do not infer a numerical energy barrier from a sketch.

answer.summary: Rotation about the ethane C-C axis keeps end-on C-C sigma overlap aligned along the internuclear axis, although conformational interactions can vary with torsion. In ethene, twisting can keep the sigma connection while rotating unhybridised p orbitals away from parallel alignment, reducing side-on pi overlap. This qualitative sketch does not determine a numerical rotational barrier.

questions.stem: A student assigns one hybridisation label to an entire molecule. Use propyne and allene to test this procedure and devise a more reliable local procedure. State the electron-domain information and orbital-consistency checks your procedure needs.

answer.summary: A molecule-wide label fails: propyne contains an sp3 methyl carbon and two sp alkyne carbons; allene contains two terminal sp2 carbons and an sp central carbon. A better procedure is atom-local: for each atom, count sigma-bond directions and lone-pair electron domains (a multiple bond is one sigma direction), assign the local introductory geometry/hybridisation, then check that enough correctly oriented unhybridised p orbitals remain for all required pi bonds/delocalisation. Revisit an assignment that fails that orbital check.

inputs: supplied benchmark stem and prior move

reasoning_route.why_valid: The introductory model describes local sigma geometry.
inputs: supplied benchmark stem and prior move

inputs: supplied benchmark stem and prior move

reasoning_route.why_valid: A local label that cannot support the required pi system is internally inconsistent.
inputs: supplied benchmark stem and prior move
